articles.originalTitle: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
articles.originalText: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.
articles.originalFullText:
1. What is Audi's $4 billion US investment plan?

US President Donald Trump announced the investment on Saturday, during a campaign rally in Georgia, a key battleground state for his Republican Party in the midterm elections next week.

Audi quickly confirmed the plan, saying it would build its first US factory near Macon, Georgia, costing around $4 billion (€3.6 billion) and creating some 4,500 jobs.

The German automaker said construction would begin next year, with a planned annual production of up to 200,000 vehicles due to start in the early 2030s.

The firm plans to build premium SUVs for the US market at the plant, marking a "long-term commitment" to what it said was "one of the world's most important premium markets."

The US investment comes as German automakers face unprecedented pressure from China, rising costs and two conflicts.

Backed by huge government subsidies, Chinese rivals have stolen a march in the transition to electric vehicles (EVs), scaling up production of new models that are fast gaining market share in a crowded global auto market.

BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Audi's parent company, Volkswagen— the world's second-largest automaker — have all issued profit warnings in recent months as margins come under pressure.

They've also announced major cost-cutting. VW is preparing to axe up to 100,000 jobs by 2030, while Audi's factory in Neckarsulm, which has around 15,000 staff, is one of four plants at risk of closure.

2. Why is Audi investing in US car production?

Trump credited his 15% tariffs on European-made vehicles for Audi's investment, saying it "would not have happened without tariffs."

While the commitment does feed into Trump's plan to bring manufacturing back to the United States from abroad, Audi said it was making the huge outlay for growth and resilience.

“We have much greater ambitions for Audi in America," said the carmaker's CEO Gernot Döllner, who appeared alongside Trump at the Republican's campaign rally.

"The United States is one of the world's most important premium markets, and we have not yet realized our full potential. We are determined to change that ... This is about building a stronger Audi business in America — not only about building a factory," he said.

However, Trump's tariffs have undoubtedly added to the automaker's woes.

Audi, which currently exports to the US market from Europe and Mexico, said the additional costs amounted to about €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) last year.

With more than 160,000 vehicles sold, Audi's US sales last year fell 16%, amid intense competition and after Trump scrapped subsidies on electric vehicles in its second-biggest market.

By building a US factory, Audi should be able to avoid or reduce Trump's tariffs, industry analysts say.

3. What is the reaction in Germany amid huge cuts in the domestic auto sector?

There's been fierce criticism of the deal due to the severe pressure facing German automakers and because the new US investment could mean further job losses at home.

Much of the criticism focused on Döllner's rally appearance alongside Trump.

The center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD)'s transport policy spokesperson Isabel Cademartori described it as campaign assistance for an autocrat who is waging a trade war against Germany.

"This is a disgrace, especially considering the history of the Volkswagen Group," she stated, referring to the party's links with Adolf Hitler's Nazi party during World War II.

Christiane Benner, president of the powerful IG Metall union, labeled the rally appearance as "extremely embarrassing, politically unacceptable and not worthy of the company."

VW works council chief Daniela Cavallo went further, saying Döllner had let himself be turned "into a puppet in [Trump's] propaganda show."

Cavallo, however, noted that the US plant could make sense from a business perspective, as VW needs to grow its market share there.

An Audi spokesperson defended the US investment, saying it was "not a decision against Germany, but rather a step toward strengthening our global competitiveness."

Manfred Döss, chairman of Audi's supervisory board, insisted the automaker's future cannot be secured by cost-cutting and efficiency alone.

"We need the courage to invest, to seize new opportunities and to make decisions that will shape our company for decades to come," he added.

4. Will Audi's investment help Trump in the US midterms?

The announcement certainly appears timed to coincide with the US midterm elections on November 3.

Voters will decide whether the Republicans or Democrats hold the balance of power in Congress during Trump's last two years in office.

Holding the announcement in the key battleground state of Georgia is seen as a strategic move to boost the fortunes of local Republican candidates.

Since he returned to the White House last year, Trump has used tariffs and political pressure to force global automakers to relocate their factories to American soil.

Audi's investment follows moves by Stellantis and Japan's Toyota to expand US production, while Honda is in talks to build a new US plant.

US auto giants General Motors and Ford have also promised to increase domestic production.

While one investment announcement may not be enough to sway many voters, it serves one of Trump's main election promises — to revive industrial production in the US.

Edited by: Rob Mudge
articles.title: Что Германия думает о сделке Audi с Трампом на $4 млрд
articles.text: Роскошный автопроизводитель собирается открыть свой первый завод в Соединенных Штатах — шаг, который Трамп приписывает своим тарифам. DW исследует реакцию Германии на массовое отключение автомобильной промышленности.
articles.fullText:
1.Каков инвестиционный план Audi на 4 миллиарда долларов США?

Президент США Дональд Трамп объявил об инвестициях в субботу во время предвыборного митинга в Грузии, ключевом штате для его Республиканской партии на промежуточных выборах на следующей неделе.

Audi быстро подтвердила план, заявив, что построит свой первый завод в США недалеко от Макона, штат Джорджия, стоимостью около 4 миллиардов долларов (3,6 миллиарда евро) и создаст около 4500 рабочих мест.

Немецкий автопроизводитель заявил, что строительство начнется в следующем году, с запланированным ежегодным производством до 200 000 автомобилей, которое должно начаться в начале 2030-х годов.

Фирма планирует построить премиальные внедорожники для рынка США на заводе, отметив «долгосрочное обязательство» к тому, что, по ее словам, было «одним из самых важных премиальных рынков в мире».

Инвестиции США приходят, когда немецкие автопроизводители сталкиваются с беспрецедентным давлением со стороны Китая, ростом расходов и двумя конфликтами.

Подкрепленные огромными государственными субсидиями, китайские конкуренты украли марш в переходе на электромобили, наращивая производство новых моделей, которые быстро набирают долю на переполненном мировом автомобильном рынке.

BMW, Mercedes-Benz и материнская компания Audi, Volkswagen, второй по величине автопроизводитель в мире, в последние месяцы выпустили предупреждения о прибыли, поскольку маржа находится под давлением.

Они также объявили о значительном сокращении расходов. VW готовится сократить до 100 000 рабочих мест к 2030 году, в то время как завод Audi в Некарсульме, штат которого насчитывает около 15 000 сотрудников, является одним из четырех заводов, находящихся под угрозой закрытия.

2.Почему Audi инвестирует в производство автомобилей в США?

Трамп отметил, что 15-процентные тарифы на автомобили европейского производства для инвестиций Audi «не могли бы произойти без тарифов».

В то время как обязательство действительно подпитывает план Трампа по возвращению производства в Соединенные Штаты из-за рубежа, Audi заявила, что делает огромные расходы на рост и устойчивость.

«У нас гораздо больше амбиций для Audi в Америке», - сказал генеральный директор автопроизводителя Гернот Дёллнер, который появился вместе с Трампом на предвыборном митинге республиканцев.

"Соединенные Штаты являются одним из важнейших мировых рынков премиальных товаров, и мы еще не полностью реализовали свой потенциал. Мы полны решимости изменить это... Речь идет о создании более сильного бизнеса Audi в Америке, а не только о строительстве завода.

Тем не менее, тарифы Трампа, несомненно, добавили проблем автопроизводителю.

Audi, которая в настоящее время экспортирует на рынок США из Европы и Мексики, заявила, что дополнительные расходы составили около 1,2 млрд евро (1,3 млрд долларов) в прошлом году.

С более чем 160 000 проданных автомобилей продажи Audi в США в прошлом году упали на 16% на фоне интенсивной конкуренции и после того, как Трамп отказался от субсидий на электромобили на своем втором по величине рынке.

По словам отраслевых аналитиков, построив завод в США, Audi должна быть в состоянии избежать или снизить тарифы Трампа.

3.Какова реакция Германии на огромные сокращения в отечественном автосекторе?

Сделка подверглась жесткой критике из-за серьезного давления, с которым сталкиваются немецкие автопроизводители, и потому, что новые инвестиции США могут привести к дальнейшим потерям рабочих мест внутри страны.

Большая часть критики была сосредоточена на выступлении Дёльнера на митинге вместе с Трампом.

Представитель левоцентристской Социал-демократической партии (СДПГ) по вопросам транспортной политики Изабель Кадемартори назвала это «помощью кампании автократу, который ведет торговую войну против Германии».

«Это позор, особенно учитывая историю Volkswagen Group», — заявила она, ссылаясь на связи партии с нацистской партией Адольфа Гитлера во время Второй мировой войны.

Президент влиятельного профсоюза IG Metall Кристиан Беннер назвала выступление на митинге «чрезвычайно неловким, политически неприемлемым и недостойным компании».

Глава совета по работе с VW Даниэла Кавалло пошла дальше, заявив, что Дёллнер позволил превратить себя «в марионетку в пропагандистском шоу [Трампа]».

Кавалло, однако, отметил, что завод в США может иметь смысл с точки зрения бизнеса, поскольку VW необходимо увеличить свою долю на рынке.

Представитель Audi заявил, что это «не решение против Германии, а скорее шаг к укреплению нашей глобальной конкурентоспособности».

Манфред Дёсс, председатель наблюдательного совета Audi, настаивал на том, что будущее автопроизводителя не может быть обеспечено только сокращением расходов и эффективностью.

Нам нужно мужество, чтобы инвестировать, использовать новые возможности и принимать решения, которые будут формировать нашу компанию на десятилетия вперед.

4. Помогут ли инвестиции Audi Трампу в промежуточных выборах в США?

Объявление, безусловно, приурочено к промежуточным выборам в США 3 ноября.

Избиратели будут решать, будут ли республиканцы или демократы удерживать баланс сил в Конгрессе в течение последних двух лет пребывания Трампа на посту.

Проведение объявления в ключевом штате Джорджия рассматривается как стратегический шаг для повышения благосостояния местных кандидатов-республиканцев.

С тех пор как Трамп вернулся в Белый дом в прошлом году, он использовал тарифы и политическое давление, чтобы заставить мировых автопроизводителей переместить свои заводы на американскую землю.

Инвестиции Audi последовали за шагами Stellantis и японской Toyota по расширению производства в США, в то время как Honda ведет переговоры о строительстве нового завода в США.

Американские автогиганты General Motors и Ford также пообещали увеличить внутреннее производство.

Хотя одного объявления об инвестициях может быть недостаточно, чтобы повлиять на многих избирателей, оно служит одному из главных предвыборных обещаний Трампа — возрождению промышленного производства в США.

Исполнитель: Rob Mudge

articles.originalTitle: Brazil elections: Merz, world leaders congratulate Lula on his win
articles.originalText: Brazilian President Lula secured a surprise win over far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, who has refused to concede. DW has the latest.
articles.originalFullText:
What you need to know

- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro

-

It was a tight runoff, with Lula winning 51.7% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.2%, official results showed

-

In his victory speech, Lula urged more regulation of big tech platforms after allegations that Meta interfered in the race

-

Trading was suspended on the stock market for half an hour on Monday morning as shares and Brazil's real currency tumbled

-

Several Latin American leaders congratulated Lula on win

-

Bolsonaro refused to concede, called for election results to be annulled

Keep reading for the latest updates from the second round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25, with continued coverage into Monday, October 26.

Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.

Recap — Why is Bolsonaro crying foul after the voting extension?

Just joining us and wondering how Brazil's runoff vote had a considerably clearer margin of victory than predicted and yet still ended in controversy and the losing candidate refusing to concede defeat?

Challenger Flavio Bolsonaro's objections were focused around the evening extension of voting past the planned closing time of 5 p.m. across the country.

The decisions by a Lula-appointed Supreme Court justice on Sunday followed a complaint over allegations of pro-Bolsonaro mayors being behind public transport irregularities that may have hampered people's plans to vote.

On election night, Bolsonaro then told journalists it was "impossible to recognize the election results, given the circumstances under which things unfolded."

For now it's unclear whether, as the dust settles, Bolsonaro will continue to resist the outcome and try to encourage protests in the way his now-jailed father Jair Bolsonaro did four years ago.

But two factors in particular seem to speak against the prospects of a potential Bolsonaro challenge.

Firstly, his fairly sizeable margin of defeat — losing by slightly more than 4 million votes rather than just a few thousand — makes it much more unlikely that a two-hour extension at polling stations could have even the theoretical potential of swaying the result.

And beyond that, his camp appealed for and successfully secured permission to keep polling stations open in some of Bolsonaro's southern strongholds, after torrential rains interfered with would-be voters' travel plans.

African leaders congratulate Lula, seek to 'advance shared interests'

Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was one of several African leaders to congratulate Lula on Monday, saying that his renewed mandate offered an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties.

"As two leading nations of the Global South, we can promote economic integration and advance our shared interests in a rapidly changing global order," Tinubu said online, saying he looked forward to expanding cooperation in a raft of areas.

Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu also extended her "sincere congratulations" to Lula.

"Tanzania values its longstanding friendship with Brazil, and looks forward to continue building on this foundation to further strengthen bilateral relations and deepen cooperation, for the mutual benefit of our two nations," Suluhu said.

Seychelles President Patrick Herminie called the runoff election result "a powerful affirmation of the trust the Brazilian people have placed in President Lula's leadership," in comments published by his office online.

He said Lula's win was "a testament to his lifelong commitment to the dignity and well-being of ordinary men and women," saying the Seychelles shared Lula's values like "social justice, equality of opportunity, the protection of workers and the most vulnerable, and a model of development that places people at its center."

Herminie expressed a desire to deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in tackling climate change, protecting the oceans and advancing the interests of the Global South.

Putin congratulates Lula, praising his 'personal contribution' to bilateral ties

Russian President Vladimir Putin offered congratulations to Lula in a telegram published by the Kremlin on Monday.

"It is difficult to overstate your personal contribution to strengthening the strategic partnership between Brazil and Russia," the telegram stated.

Putin, a leader of a fellow BRICS alliance member, is one of few world leaders to have worked with Lula across all of his presidential terms, starting in 2003.

Putin also congratulated Lula on his upcoming 81st birthday, which falls on Tuesday.

The Russian president's spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow earlier in the day that the Kremlin welcomed Lula's re-election.

WATCH: Brazil's Lula celebrates election victory as Bolsonaro rejects results

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term after defeating far-right rival Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff election.

It's a historic political comeback for Lula who trailed in the first round.

DW reports from Rio de Janeiro.

Sao Paulo stock exchange halts trading over sharp drop after Lula win

Trading on the Sao Paulo stock exchange, the largest in Latin America, was suspended for 30 minutes on Monday after plummeting nearly 17% in the wake of the re-election of left-wing Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who defeated conservative Flavio Bolsonaro.

The sharp drop in the benchmark Ibovespa index triggered a 30-minute "circuit breaker" mechanism provided for "periods of sharp market decline," according to a stock exchange statement.

Meanwhile, the US dollar surged 12% against Brazil's currency, one of the real's biggest daily moves on record.

Prices of raw sugar, one of Brazil's most important exports, slid nearly 5% on the collapsing exchange rate.

Prediction markets had indicated a Bolsonaro win but the right-wing senator's refusal to concede defeat and his pledge to challenge the election result have added to investor uncertainty.

"Important for local financial markets will be how quickly Bolsonaro accepts the result, or at least allows the constitution to run its course," Chris Turner, a strategist at ING in London, told the Reuters news agency as attention turned to Lula's choice of finance minister — a clue as to his fiscal approach.

"The key signal for markets will be the next Lula administration's commitment to fiscal discipline, starting with the appointment of a new finance minister in coming weeks," RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Graham Stock told Reuters.

Germany's Merz wants to deepen 'the strategic partnership' with Brazil

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has joined the chorus of world leaders congratulating Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election.

"I look forward to further deepening the strategic partnership between Germany and Brazil together," Merz said in a message posted on X.

Germany and Brazil held government consultations in Hannover in April of this year, at which Merz and Lula agreed to cooperate more closely on defense and raw materials, among other things.

Brazilian markets poised for sharp drop Monday after Lula win

Brazilian markets are bracing for heavy selling on Monday, with futures of Brazil's benchmark stock index Bovespa falling nearly 15% in early Monday trading

On global markets, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, which tracks a basket of major Brazilian stocks, plunged as much as 26% in premarket trading as investors unwind bets on a right-wing victory.

Brazilian Real November futures also fell 10% in Asian trading, while US-listed shares of Brazilian stocks dropped as well, with energy giant Petrobras plunging more than 20% and banking group Itau Unibanco cratering almost 30%.

Investors had seen election loser Flavio Bolsonaro as the candidate most likely to boost markets with fiscal austerity and deregulation, while Lula has pursued policies of redistribution and state-led development, including costly welfare programs.

Russia says it welcomes Lula's re-election

The Kremlin said on Monday it welcomed Lula's victory and praised what it said were his efforts to cultivate Brazil-Russia ties.

"We welcome Mr. Lula's victory. He does a lot, not only for the development of bilateral relations but also for advancing processes within the framework of BRICS," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

He said Russia hoped for more of the same.

Lula himself has possibly put Brazil in the Kremlin's good books by not joining Western sanctions on Russia over Moscow's invasion of Ukraine and calling for a negotiated peace.

However, he has called on all nations to adhere to the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity enshrined in the UN Charter, thus implicitly condemning Russia's aggression.

Brazil and Russia are both members of BRICS, an international cooperation group founded in 2009 along with India and China, with South Africa joining a year later, and taking all those countries' first initials to make up its name.

It has since then been expanded to include 10 member nations in all, with a number of "partner countries" also invited in 2024.

Votes tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close

Here's a DW infographic on where the results stand:

France, China, Spain congratulate Lula on victory

Messages of congratulations continue to rain in from around the world following Lula's unexpected win.

China's response was measured, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying that "China has noted that Brazil's Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations."

Guo added that Beijing was "willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future."

French President Emmanuel Macron, after expressing his congratulations, said Brazil and France should work to "strengthen our strategic partnership."

"France and Brazil have much to build together," Macron said X, adding that the two countries should nurture their friendship "in the service of a fairer world."

Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, was more effusive, casting Lula's victory as evidence that the world is experiencing a backlash to its seeming rightwards political trajectory at present.

"A great victory for Lula! What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The global progressive comeback has just begun," Sanchez, who has called snap elections in November, posted on X.

Big challenges face Lula's fourth term

Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is likely to face several difficulties in enacting his agenda in a fourth-term.

Among other things, Brazil has elected its most conservative congress since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s.

Flavio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allies could control more than 280 seats in the 513-seat lower house and up to 50 seats in the 81-seat Senate following parliamentary elections three weeks ago.

This could lead to Lula's being forced to cede to congress on decisions about the budget, important legislation and key nominations.

Economic woes

Brazil is also in a period of weak economic growth, with his government forecasting just a 2.3% rise in GDP next year.

This is combined with public debt that surpasses 82% of GDP, the highest rate since the coronavirus pandemic.

Security concerns

Public security also remains a major concern in Brazil, with criminal organizations holding considerable influence in parts of the country.

Lula has said he plans to establish a Ministry of Public Security to combat the problem.

Environmental problems

There are also environmental challenges ahead.

Although deforestation in the Amazon — a major carbon sink and thus vital for the stability of the world climate — fell significantly during Lula's third term, Brazil is still a long way from its goal of ending deforestation by 2030.

EU's von der Leyen hails Lula's win

The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, has posted an online message of congratulation to "my friend" Lula on his win in Brazil's election runoff.

"Democracy and multilateralism have won in Brazil," she wrote.

"Europe's partnership with Brazil is thriving. We will remain by your side for the years to come," her post continued.

"Together we will keep working closely for free and open trade. A rules-based global order. And strong ambitions for our climate."

Could Bolsonaro succeed in annulling the vote?

Some uncertainty still surrounds the final result of Brazil's election, as Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to challenge the outcome over the two-hour extension of polling hours ordered by a Supreme Court judge at the request of Lula da Silva's campaign.

However, legal experts have expressed doubt as to whether such a complaint would meet the legal threshold for the election to be annulled.

Bolsonaro's case would be weakened by at least two factors, analysts said. Firstly, the scale of his loss to Lula and second, the fact that his campaign had also requested an extension in some states.

The president of the electoral court, Kassio Nunes Marques, said that the extension of voting hours had not influenced the vote.

The Associated Press cited Joao Pedro Padua, a law professor at Brazil's Fluminense Federal University, as saying that Bolsonaro could ask for the elections to be declared null and void by filing a complaint with electoral authorities or the Supreme Court.

"But there isn't much legal basis for that," Padua said.

"The extension of voting hours is unusual, but for it to invalidate the elections, the candidate would have to prove that it affected voters' ability to freely express their will. There doesn't seem to have been any such impact," he said.

Shortly before scheduled voting ended, Supreme Court Judge Christiano had ordered polling stations to remain open for longer after problems with public transport were reported to be affecting voters.

The decision followed a request from Lula's campaign.

Bolsonaro's campaign had also called for an extension of voting hours but only in some conservative-leaning southern states hit by heavy rainfall, flooding and power outages that were said to be disrupting voting.

Flavio Bolsonaro rejects defeat, seeks annulment of Brazil election

Right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has rejected his defeat to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential run-off, calling for the election to be annulled over a two-hour extension of voting hours.

Speaking to reporters after the electoral court declared Lula the winner, Bolsonaro said he could not accept the result. He criticized a decision by Supreme Court judge Cristiano Zanin to extend voting hours nationwide, arguing that it had changed the rules of the election.

"What happened today was not normal. It was unacceptable," Bolsonaro said, arguing that the nationwide extension had undermined equal treatment between states. He said he would take legal action against the result.

Lula’s campaign had requested the extension, citing difficulties transporting voters to polling stations in several states. Bolsonaro’s campaign had also sought extra voting time, but only in municipalities across five states, citing heavy rain, flooding and power outages.

Lula says Brazilians voted to defend democracy, vows to resist US influence

Brazilians voted to "guarantee democracy," President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Sunday after beating Flavio Bolsonaro to win an unprecedented fourth term.

In a post on X, Lula thanked Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets in defense of democracy, saying: "This victory belongs to a people who believe, who fight, and who never give up on building a more just, sovereign, and democratic Brazil."

In his victory speech, Lula reiterated that Brazil would "not accept being anyone’s backyard," a recurring campaign message defending the country’s sovereignty against US influence. The stance may have helped him win votes, with some voters viewing Washington’s actions as interference.

Relations between the two countries deteriorated in 2025, when the US imposed tariffs on Brazil in retaliation for legal proceedings against former president Jair Bolsonaro, who was later convicted of coup-plotting.

Speaking in a hoarse voice, Lula thanked his campaign team and Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets to defend democracy. He described the result as a "loss for negativity, lies."

The re-elected president also promised better regulation of big tech platforms, after Meta was the subject of legal complaints over alleged "interference" throughout the polarizing campaign.

Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was one of several African leaders to congratulate Lula on Monday, saying that his renewed mandate offered an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties.

"As two leading nations of the Global South, we can promote economic integration and advance our shared interests in a rapidly changing global order," Tinubu said online, saying he looked forward to expanding cooperation in a raft of areas.

Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu also extended her "sincere congratulations" to Lula.

"Tanzania values its longstanding friendship with Brazil, and looks forward to continue building on this foundation to further strengthen bilateral relations and deepen cooperation, for the mutual benefit of our two nations," Suluhu said.

Seychelles President Patrick Herminie called the runoff election result "a powerful affirmation of the trust the Brazilian people have placed in President Lula's leadership," in comments published by his office online.

He said Lula's win was "a testament to his lifelong commitment to the dignity and well-being of ordinary men and women," saying the Seychelles shared Lula's values like "social justice, equality of opportunity, the protection of workers and the most vulnerable, and a model of development that places people at its center."

Herminie expressed a desire to deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in tackling climate change, protecting the oceans and advancing the interests of the Global South.

Putin congratulates Lula, praising his 'personal contribution' to bilateral ties

Russian President Vladimir Putin offered congratulations to Lula in a telegram published by the Kremlin on Monday.

"It is difficult to overstate your personal contribution to strengthening the strategic partnership between Brazil and Russia," the telegram stated.

Putin, a leader of a fellow BRICS alliance member, is one of few world leaders to have worked with Lula across all of his presidential terms, starting in 2003.

Putin also congratulated Lula on his upcoming 81st birthday, which falls on Tuesday.

The Russian president's spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow earlier in the day that the Kremlin welcomed Lula's re-election.

WATCH: Brazil's Lula celebrates election victory as Bolsonaro rejects results

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term after defeating far-right rival Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff election.

It's a historic political comeback for Lula who trailed in the first round.

DW reports from Rio de Janeiro.

Sao Paulo stock exchange halts trading over sharp drop after Lula win

Trading on the Sao Paulo stock exchange, the largest in Latin America, was suspended for 30 minutes on Monday after plummeting nearly 17% in the wake of the re-election of left-wing Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who defeated conservative Flavio Bolsonaro.

The sharp drop in the benchmark Ibovespa index triggered a 30-minute "circuit breaker" mechanism provided for "periods of sharp market decline," according to a stock exchange statement.

Meanwhile, the US dollar surged 12% against Brazil's currency, one of the real's biggest daily moves on record.

Prices of raw sugar, one of Brazil's most important exports, slid nearly 5% on the collapsing exchange rate.

Prediction markets had indicated a Bolsonaro win but the right-wing senator's refusal to concede defeat and his pledge to challenge the election result have added to investor uncertainty.

"Important for local financial markets will be how quickly Bolsonaro accepts the result, or at least allows the constitution to run its course," Chris Turner, a strategist at ING in London, told the Reuters news agency as attention turned to Lula's choice of finance minister — a clue as to his fiscal approach.

"The key signal for markets will be the next Lula administration's commitment to fiscal discipline, starting with the appointment of a new finance minister in coming weeks," RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Graham Stock told Reuters.

Germany's Merz wants to deepen 'the strategic partnership' with Brazil

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has joined the chorus of world leaders congratulating Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election.

"I look forward to further deepening the strategic partnership between Germany and Brazil together," Merz said in a message posted on X.

Germany and Brazil held government consultations in Hannover in April of this year, at which Merz and Lula agreed to cooperate more closely on defense and raw materials, among other things.

Brazilian markets poised for sharp drop Monday after Lula win

Brazilian markets are bracing for heavy selling on Monday, with futures of Brazil's benchmark stock index Bovespa falling nearly 15% in early Monday trading

On global markets, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, which tracks a basket of major Brazilian stocks, plunged as much as 26% in premarket trading as investors unwind bets on a right-wing victory.

Brazilian Real November futures also fell 10% in Asian trading, while US-listed shares of Brazilian stocks dropped as well, with energy giant Petrobras plunging more than 20% and banking group Itau Unibanco cratering almost 30%.

Investors had seen election loser Flavio Bolsonaro as the candidate most likely to boost markets with fiscal austerity and deregulation, while Lula has pursued policies of redistribution and state-led development, including costly welfare programs.

Russia says it welcomes Lula's re-election

The Kremlin said on Monday it welcomed Lula's victory and praised what it said were his efforts to cultivate Brazil-Russia ties.

"We welcome Mr. Lula's victory. He does a lot, not only for the development of bilateral relations but also for advancing processes within the framework of BRICS," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

He said Russia hoped for more of the same.

Lula himself has possibly put Brazil in the Kremlin's good books by not joining Western sanctions on Russia over Moscow's invasion of Ukraine and calling for a negotiated peace.

However, he has called on all nations to adhere to the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity enshrined in the UN Charter, thus implicitly condemning Russia's aggression.

Brazil and Russia are both members of BRICS, an international cooperation group founded in 2009 along with India and China, with South Africa joining a year later, and taking all those countries' first initials to make up its name.

It has since then been expanded to include 10 member nations in all, with a number of "partner countries" also invited in 2024.

Votes tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close

Here's a DW infographic on where the results stand:

France, China, Spain congratulate Lula on victory

Messages of congratulations continue to rain in from around the world following Lula's unexpected win.

China's response was measured, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying that "China has noted that Brazil's Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations."

Guo added that Beijing was "willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future."

French President Emmanuel Macron, after expressing his congratulations, said Brazil and France should work to "strengthen our strategic partnership."

"France and Brazil have much to build together," Macron said X, adding that the two countries should nurture their friendship "in the service of a fairer world."

Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, was more effusive, casting Lula's victory as evidence that the world is experiencing a backlash to its seeming rightwards political trajectory at present.

"A great victory for Lula! What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The global progressive comeback has just begun," Sanchez, who has called snap elections in November, posted on X.

Big challenges face Lula's fourth term

Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is likely to face several difficulties in enacting his agenda in a fourth-term.

Among other things, Brazil has elected its most conservative congress since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s.

Flavio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allies could control more than 280 seats in the 513-seat lower house and up to 50 seats in the 81-seat Senate following parliamentary elections three weeks ago.

This could lead to Lula's being forced to cede to congress on decisions about the budget, important legislation and key nominations.

Economic woes

Brazil is also in a period of weak economic growth, with his government forecasting just a 2.3% rise in GDP next year.

This is combined with public debt that surpasses 82% of GDP, the highest rate since the coronavirus pandemic.

Security concerns

Public security also remains a major concern in Brazil, with criminal organizations holding considerable influence in parts of the country.

Lula has said he plans to establish a Ministry of Public Security to combat the problem.

Environmental problems

There are also environmental challenges ahead.

Although deforestation in the Amazon — a major carbon sink and thus vital for the stability of the world climate — fell significantly during Lula's third term, Brazil is still a long way from its goal of ending deforestation by 2030.

EU's von der Leyen hails Lula's win

The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, has posted an online message of congratulation to "my friend" Lula on his win in Brazil's election runoff.

"Democracy and multilateralism have won in Brazil," she wrote.

"Europe's partnership with Brazil is thriving. We will remain by your side for the years to come," her post continued.

"Together we will keep working closely for free and open trade. A rules-based global order. And strong ambitions for our climate."

Could Bolsonaro succeed in annulling the vote?

Some uncertainty still surrounds the final result of Brazil's election, as Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to challenge the outcome over the two-hour extension of polling hours ordered by a Supreme Court judge at the request of Lula da Silva's campaign.

However, legal experts have expressed doubt as to whether such a complaint would meet the legal threshold for the election to be annulled.

Bolsonaro's case would be weakened by at least two factors, analysts said. Firstly, the scale of his loss to Lula and second, the fact that his campaign had also requested an extension in some states.

The president of the electoral court, Kassio Nunes Marques, said that the extension of voting hours had not influenced the vote.

The Associated Press cited Joao Pedro Padua, a law professor at Brazil's Fluminense Federal University, as saying that Bolsonaro could ask for the elections to be declared null and void by filing a complaint with electoral authorities or the Supreme Court.

"But there isn't much legal basis for that," Padua said.

"The extension of voting hours is unusual, but for it to invalidate the elections, the candidate would have to prove that it affected voters' ability to freely express their will. There doesn't seem to have been any such impact," he said.

Shortly before scheduled voting ended, Supreme Court Judge Christiano had ordered polling stations to remain open for longer after problems with public transport were reported to be affecting voters.

The decision followed a request from Lula's campaign.

Bolsonaro's campaign had also called for an extension of voting hours but only in some conservative-leaning southern states hit by heavy rainfall, flooding and power outages that were said to be disrupting voting.

Flavio Bolsonaro rejects defeat, seeks annulment of Brazil election

Right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has rejected his defeat to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential run-off, calling for the election to be annulled over a two-hour extension of voting hours.

Speaking to reporters after the electoral court declared Lula the winner, Bolsonaro said he could not accept the result. He criticized a decision by Supreme Court judge Cristiano Zanin to extend voting hours nationwide, arguing that it had changed the rules of the election.

"What happened today was not normal. It was unacceptable," Bolsonaro said, arguing that the nationwide extension had undermined equal treatment between states. He said he would take legal action against the result.

Lula’s campaign had requested the extension, citing difficulties transporting voters to polling stations in several states. Bolsonaro’s campaign had also sought extra voting time, but only in municipalities across five states, citing heavy rain, flooding and power outages.

Lula says Brazilians voted to defend democracy, vows to resist US influence

Brazilians voted to "guarantee democracy," President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Sunday after beating Flavio Bolsonaro to win an unprecedented fourth term.

In a post on X, Lula thanked Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets in defense of democracy, saying: "This victory belongs to a people who believe, who fight, and who never give up on building a more just, sovereign, and democratic Brazil."

In his victory speech, Lula reiterated that Brazil would "not accept being anyone’s backyard," a recurring campaign message defending the country’s sovereignty against US influence. The stance may have helped him win votes, with some voters viewing Washington’s actions as interference.

Relations between the two countries deteriorated in 2025, when the US imposed tariffs on Brazil in retaliation for legal proceedings against former president Jair Bolsonaro, who was later convicted of coup-plotting.

Speaking in a hoarse voice, Lula thanked his campaign team and Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets to defend democracy. He described the result as a "loss for negativity, lies."

The re-elected president also promised better regulation of big tech platforms, after Meta was the subject of legal complaints over alleged "interference" throughout the polarizing campaign.

articles.originalTitle: Why Ukraine may be involved in Mali's conflict
articles.originalText: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe.
articles.originalFullText:
Ukraine is fighting Russia — and the conflict may extend into Africa's Sahel region.

According to an investigation published by US media outlet CNN in September, around 15 Ukrainian drone specialists are reportedly supporting Tuareg rebels in northern Mali. Their common enemy: the military government in Bamako and its Russian allies.

But how reliable is the information? And what price could Kyiv pay for engaging in Africa?

Marta Oliynyk-D'omochko, coordinator of the African Studies Program at the National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy, sees a strategic motive. "Ukraine's main interest is to weaken Russia's influence around the world," she told DW. If Russia's military influence were rolled back, she added, the economic opportunities arising from it would also diminish.

Russian historian Irina Filatova, professor emeritus at the University of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa, also considers Ukrainian support for the Tuareg movement plausible. However, she said she has no independent evidence to confirm such involvement.

Kyiv's alleged partners are controversial. The Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) cooperates with the Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimeen (JNIM), a jihadist group affiliated with al-Qaeda.

Suspicions dating back to 2024

In July 2024, DW reported on possible involvement by the Ukrainian military intelligence service (HUR) in an ambush on Russian Wagner fighters near Tinzaouaten in northern Mali.

At the time, HUR spokesperson Andriy Yusov said the Tuareg rebels had received information they needed to carry out the attack. Ukraine denied direct involvement.

Paramilitaries from Russia's Wagner Group and Malian troops suffered heavy losses in the July 2024 attack.

CNN's investigation has reignited the question of whether the Russia-Ukraine war is also being fought on African soil.

Signals from Kyiv, but no confirmation

The suspicions were renewed by a post on X by Kyrylo Budanov. The former head of Ukraine's military intelligence, now chief of staff to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, wrote on September 7 that Ukrainian intelligence protects the country's interests worldwide — "from Russia to Africa … in the burning desert sands and in the snows of icy Antarctica...".

Budanov did not explicitly mention Mali and his post does not confirm any specific operation. CNN reported that the Ukrainians provided drone training, operational planning and remote support for drone missions. DW has not independently verified those claims.

DW reached out to the HUR for comment. Among other things, DW wanted to know whether personnel had been deployed to Mali, whether the political leadership had approved such a mission, and what measures were in place to ensure that the JNIM — which cooperates with the FLA — does not indirectly benefit from Ukrainian support.

DW did not receive a specific response. An HUR spokesperson said the agency might provide information at a later date. The extent of any potential Ukrainian involvement therefore remains unclear.

Why Mali matters to Kyiv

Following military coups in 2020 and 2021, Mali increasingly turned away from Western partners and toward Russia. The Wagner Group was subsequently replaced by the Africa Corps in 2025 as Moscow reorganized its military presence.

Russia has sought to consolidate its influence in the Sahel region and present itself as a reliable security partner.

Ulf Laessing, former head of the Sahel program of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation in Mali and now head of its Syria and Iraq program, said Russia is continuing to expand its activities in Africa.

"I have received information that the Africa Corps still uses Syria and Libya as transit points for flights from Russia, including for refueling and loading, to support its operations on the continent," Laessing told DW.

From Ukraine's perspective, it could be attractive to exert pressure on Russian forces in Africa.

Filatova sees a strategic logic to this: "The Ukrainians regard Russian troops anywhere in the world as legitimate targets." Setbacks in Mali could tie up Russian resources and undermine Moscow's reputation as a security partner, she argued.

However, Oliynyk-D'omochko stressed that the relationship with the Tuareg is not a comprehensive alliance. The FLA is not seeking to replace the government in Bamako. Instead, it is focused on northern Mali and is pursuing self-determination or extensive autonomy.

Oliynyk-D'omochko describes the relationship as a tactical arrangement: "It is more of a situational alliance against a common enemy than a comprehensive partnership."

The alliance with jihadists

The FLA is fighting for an independent state in the north of Mali, a region predominantly inhabited by Tuaregs. JNIM, by contrast, aims to impose strict Islamic rule. Both groups oppose the military government and its Russian allies, but their objectives differ.

Any potential Ukrainian support for the FLA would not, in itself, prove that Kyiv is directly supporting JNIM. However, jihadists could benefit indirectly if they conduct joint operations with FLA or gain access to knowledge and equipment.

Cooperation between Tuareg and Islamist groups dates back more than a decade.

After the ousting and killing of Libya's longtime dictator Muammar al-Gaddafi during the Arab Spring in October 2011, heavily armed Tuareg fighters returned to Mali and took up the struggle for an independent state.

In the process, separatist ambitions became intertwined with Islamist movements. Iyad Ag Ghaly, the current leader of JNIM, was himself involved in the Tuareg rebellion before turning to jihadism.

According to Oliynyk-D'omochko, the cooperation is primarily tactical in nature. The two sides have collaborated during past uprisings but later fell out. It remains unclear how long the current alliance will last.

For Kyiv, this also poses a political risk. In many African countries, the Tuaregs are viewed as separatists. Cooperation with them could therefore create the impression that Ukraine is interfering in another country's internal affairs.

Claims of support for armed groups

Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso accuse Ukraine of supporting armed groups and threatening their territorial integrity. The three Sahel nations, all ruled by military governments, have severed diplomatic relations with Kyiv and deepened their cooperation with Russia.

In September, Mali's Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop accused Ukraine at the United Nations of "providing clear and open support to terrorist groups and other mafia-like groups to undermine our country's territorial integrity," reported Agence France-Presse. Diop did not provide evidence for his claim.

The three nations' governments have may have an interest in legitimizing their partnership with Moscow and portraying Kyiv as a destabilizing actor.

Oliynyk-D'omochko has found no definitive proof of the allegations, yet warned of the potential consequences for Ukraine's Africa policy. Kyiv advocates equal partnerships with African countries. Any alleged cooperation with separatists could undermine that message and affect how potential partners view Ukraine.

What price could Ukraine pay?

Engagement in Mali could offer Ukraine a relatively low-cost way to weaken Russian interests beyond Europe. A small team of specialists could train local fighters and improve their capabilities in the use of drones.

But a potential partnership with the FLA carries political risks. Because the Tuareg separatists cooperate with the JNIM, Kyiv could face accusations of indirectly supporting jihadist fighters. That could undermine Ukraine's efforts to strengthen its relations with African countries.

This article has been translated from German

Correction, October 26, 2026: An earlier version of this article stated that the CNN investigation was published in October 2026; the report was published in September. DW apologizes for the error.
articles.title: Почему Украина может быть вовлечена в конфликт в Мали
articles.text: Утверждения о том, что украинские специалисты поддерживают повстанцев-туарегов в Мали, свидетельствуют о том, что Киев пытается бросить вызов российскому влиянию далеко за пределами поля боя в Европе.
articles.fullText:
Украина воюет с Россией, и конфликт может распространиться на африканский регион Сахель.

Согласно расследованию, опубликованному американским СМИ CNN в сентябре, около 15 украинских специалистов по беспилотникам поддерживают повстанцев-туарегов на севере Мали. Их общий враг: военное правительство в Бамако и его российские союзники.

Насколько надежна информация? И какую цену может заплатить Киев за участие в Африке?

Марта Олийник-Домочко, координатор Программы африканских исследований Национального университета Киево-Могилянской академии, видит стратегический мотив. «Основной интерес Украины заключается в ослаблении влияния России во всем мире», — сказала она. Если военное влияние России будет сведено на нет, экономические возможности, вытекающие из этого, также уменьшатся.

Российский историк Ирина Филатова, почетный профессор Университета Квазулу-Натал в Южной Африке, также считает правдоподобной украинскую поддержку движения туарегов. Однако она заявила, что у нее нет независимых доказательств, подтверждающих такую причастность.

Предполагаемые партнеры Киева являются спорными. Туарегский сепаратистский Фронт освобождения Азавада (ФЛА) сотрудничает с Джамаат Нусрат аль-Ислам валь Муслимин (JNIM), джихадистской группой, связанной с Аль-Каидой.

Подозрения восходят к 2024 году

В июле 2024 года DW сообщил о возможном участии украинской военной разведки (HUR) в засаде на российских бойцов Вагнера близ Тинзауатена на севере Мали.

В то время пресс-секретарь ХУР Андрей Юсов заявил, что туарегские повстанцы получили информацию, необходимую им для проведения атаки. Украина отрицает свою прямую причастность.

Военные группы Вагнера и малийские войска понесли тяжелые потери в результате нападения в июле 2024 года.

Расследование CNN вновь подняло вопрос о том, ведется ли российско-украинская война на африканской земле.

Сигналы из Киева, но подтверждения нет

Подозрения возобновил пост на Х Кирилл Буданов. Бывший глава военной разведки Украины, ныне начальник штаба президента Владимира Зеленского, 7 сентября написал, что украинская разведка защищает интересы страны во всем мире — «от России до Африки... в горящих пустынных песках и в снегах ледяной Антарктиды...».

Буданов прямо не упомянул Мали и его пост не подтверждает какую-либо конкретную операцию. CNN сообщает, что украинцы обеспечивали обучение беспилотников, оперативное планирование и удаленную поддержку миссий беспилотников. DW не проверяла эти утверждения.

DW обратился в HUR за комментариями. Среди прочего, DW хотел знать, был ли персонал развернут в Мали, одобрило ли политическое руководство такую миссию и какие меры были приняты для обеспечения того, чтобы JNIM, который сотрудничает с FLA, не получал косвенной поддержки со стороны Украины.

DW не получил конкретного ответа. Представитель HUR сказал, что агентство может предоставить информацию позже. Степень потенциального участия Украины остается неясной.

Почему Мали имеет значение для Киева

После военных переворотов в 2020 и 2021 годах Мали все чаще отворачивался от западных партнеров и в сторону России. Группа Вагнера была заменена Корпусом Африки в 2025 году, когда Москва реорганизовала свое военное присутствие.

Россия стремится укрепить свое влияние в Сахельском регионе и представить себя надежным партнером по безопасности.

Ульф Лассинг, бывший руководитель программы «Сахель» Фонда Конрада Аденауэра в Мали, а ныне глава программы «Сирия и Ирак», заявил, что Россия продолжает расширять свою деятельность в Африке.

«Я получил информацию о том, что Африканский корпус по-прежнему использует Сирию и Ливию в качестве транзитных пунктов для полетов из России, в том числе для дозаправки и погрузки, для поддержки своих операций на континенте», — сказал он.

С точки зрения Украины, было бы привлекательно оказывать давление на российские силы в Африке.

Филатова видит в этом стратегическую логику: "Украинцы считают российские войска в любой точке мира законными целями". По ее мнению, неудачи в Мали могут связать российские ресурсы и подорвать репутацию Москвы как партнера по безопасности.

Однако Олийник-Домочко подчеркнул, что отношения с туарегами не являются всеобъемлющим альянсом. ФЛА не стремится заменить правительство в Бамако. Вместо этого она сосредоточена на севере Мали и стремится к самоопределению или широкой автономии.

Олейник-Домочко описывает отношения как тактическую договоренность: «Это скорее ситуационный союз против общего врага, чем всеобъемлющее партнерство».

Союз с джихадистами

FLA борется за независимое государство на севере Мали, в регионе, населенном преимущественно туарегами. JNIM, напротив, стремится установить строгое исламское правление. Обе группы выступают против военного правительства и его российских союзников, но их цели различаются.

Любая потенциальная украинская поддержка ФЛА сама по себе не докажет, что Киев напрямую поддерживает СНМ. Однако джихадисты могут получить косвенную выгоду, если они проведут совместные операции с ФЛА или получат доступ к знаниям и оборудованию.

Сотрудничество между туарегами и исламистскими группировками насчитывает более десяти лет.

После свержения и убийства диктатора Ливии Муаммара Каддафи во время Арабской весны в октябре 2011 года тяжеловооруженные туареги вернулись в Мали и занялись борьбой за независимое государство.

В процессе сепаратистские амбиции переплетались с исламистскими движениями. Ияд Аг Гали, нынешний лидер JNIM, сам участвовал в восстании туарегов, прежде чем перейти к джихадизму.

По словам Олейник-Домочко, сотрудничество носит прежде всего тактический характер. Обе стороны сотрудничали во время прошлых восстаний, но позже выпали. Остается неясным, как долго продлится нынешний альянс.

Для Киева это также представляет политический риск. Во многих африканских странах туареги считаются сепаратистами. Поэтому сотрудничество с ними может создать впечатление, что Украина вмешивается во внутренние дела другой страны.

Заявления о поддержке вооруженных групп

Мали, Нигер и Буркина-Фасо обвиняют Украину в поддержке вооруженных группировок и угрозе их территориальной целостности. Три сахельских государства, управляемые военными правительствами, разорвали дипломатические отношения с Киевом и углубили сотрудничество с Россией.

В сентябре министр иностранных дел Мали Абдулайе Диоп обвинил Украину в Организации Объединенных Наций в «оказании явной и открытой поддержки террористическим группам и другим мафиозным группам, чтобы подорвать территориальную целостность нашей страны», сообщает агентство France-Presse. Диоп не предоставил доказательств своего утверждения.

Правительства трех стран могут быть заинтересованы в легитимизации своего партнерства с Москвой и изображении Киева как дестабилизирующего игрока.

Олийник-Домочко не нашел окончательных доказательств этих обвинений, но предупредил о возможных последствиях для политики Украины в Африке. Киев выступает за равноправное партнерство с африканскими странами. Любое предполагаемое сотрудничество с сепаратистами может подорвать это сообщение и повлиять на то, как потенциальные партнеры рассматривают Украину.

Какую цену может заплатить Украина?

Участие в Мали может предложить Украине относительно недорогой способ ослабить российские интересы за пределами Европы. Небольшая команда специалистов могла бы обучать местных бойцов и улучшать их возможности в использовании беспилотников.

Но потенциальное партнерство с ФЛА несет политические риски. Поскольку туарегские сепаратисты сотрудничают с СНМ, Киев может столкнуться с обвинениями в косвенной поддержке боевиков-джихадистов. Это может подорвать усилия Украины по укреплению отношений с африканскими странами.

articles.originalTitle: Новые власти Сербии отказались вводить санкции против России
articles.originalFullText:
Победившее на выборах в Сербии движение «Студенческий список — Студенты побеждают» не будет вводить санкции против России. Об этом заявил представитель блока Йово Бакич, его слова приводит RT Balkan.

«Мы уважаем Россию и как великую державу, и как нашего исторически важного партнера, а во многих случаях — и защитника. Никаких изменений в этом вопросе не будет», — сказал он.

Бакич заверил, что новое сербское правительство не будет вводить санкции против Москвы. По его словам, такой шаг может нанести ущерб историческим отношениям двух стран.

Представитель победившего в Сербии движения добавил, что страна «пережила санкции ООН и прекрасно знает, какое это испытание».

25 октября в Сербии прошли досрочные парламентские выборы. Неожиданно для экспертов и жителей страны победу одержало оппозиционное движение «Студенческий список — Студенты побеждают».

articles.originalTitle: Лавров обсудил с главой МИД Словакии урегулирование на Украине
articles.originalFullText:
Министр иностранных дел России Сергей Лавров провел переговоры с главой МИД Словакии Юраем Бланаром. Стороны обменялись мнениями по украинскому урегулированию и обсудили кризисное состояние отношений Москвы и Брюсселя. Об этом сообщили в российском дипведомстве.

Глава словацкого МИД прибыл в российскую столицу во главе делегации для участия в 22-м заседании двусторонней Межправительственной комиссии по экономическому и научно-техническому сотрудничеству.

«В конструктивном ключе обсужден ряд практических вопросов российско-словацких связей, перспективы развития политического диалога, взаимодействия в торгово-экономической, культурно-гуманитарной и военно-мемориальной сферах», — отметили в российском внешнеполитическом ведомстве.

Ранее Лавров заявил, что страны Запада больше никогда не будут главными игроками на международной арене. По его мнению, мир развернулся в другую сторону, а «исторический процесс объективно делает экономику, политику и мировые финансы совершенно другими».

Из-за этого, отметил Лавров, западные страны идут на беспрецедентные авантюры. В качестве примера он привел похищение президента Венесуэлы Николаса Мадуро. Лавров добавил, что Россия, напротив, выступает за равноправный диалог и баланс интересов в международных отношениях.

articles.originalTitle: AI giant Anthropic files for an IPO that could break records
articles.originalText: The AI company, which makes the popular Claude chatbot, has filed for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest ever.
articles.originalFullText:
The artificial intelligence startup Anthropic, maker of the hugely popular Claude AI models, has taken a major step toward holding an initial public offering that analysts expect to be one of the biggest ever.

Anthropic filed final paperwork with regulators on Monday for an IPO under the ticker symbol ANT that reports have said could value the company at between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.

That would put it in league with Elon Musk's rocketry and AI company SpaceX, which was valued at around $1.8 trillion when it listed in June. Anthropic's listing prospectus did not say how many shares the company will offer or at what price range.

The filing of a public version of a registration statement called a Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission is a major milestone in Anthropic's meteoric rise. It was launched just five years ago by a breakaway group of OpenAI researchers, led by Dario Amodei, who were concerned that that company, run by Sam Altman, was not on a path to develop AI safely.

Anthropic has since become a juggernaut, and OpenAI's biggest competitor, with some of the most widely used AI models on the market. But the company has faced controversy, including a conflict with the Pentagon over how its models can be used and questions about Amodei's dire warnings on AI risks.

AI stocks have been hit by volatility

The filing comes at a volatile time in the stock market for AI-related companies, as investors waver between exuberance about the positive effects AI could have on the economy and concern about safety and the tsunami of investment in the technology.

The IPO, which could happen as soon as November, will be one of the most eagerly anticipated public share offerings in years. OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, is also planning an IPO, but those plans are temporarily on ice, with Altman ruling out a listing this year as "ill-advised" in the face of swirling AI safety concerns.

"Going public has a lot of advantages. It brings in capital for growth. It makes it easier for you to raise additional capital elsewhere. And it makes it possible for your existing investors to cash out," said Jim Angel, an associate professor and markets specialist at Georgetown University.

But, he added, "there's concern that we may be in an AI bubble. We're in a very dynamic industry, to say the least, and we can expect a lot of volatility in the markets." Still, Angel said, it makes sense for Anthropic to "strike while the iron is hot" and list shares now to get as high a valuation as possible.

With SpaceX already trading publicly, Anthropic's IPO could test investor appetite for AI businesses at a time when markets are jittery about whether they can be profitable enough to justify the mind-boggling sums of money being invested in AI. SpaceX's shares soared briefly after the listing, but have come back down to around $150, where they started trading.

Concerns remain about the AI sector

The balancing act for companies trying to ride the AI wave is real. The data center and infrastructure provider CoreWeave saw its share price plummet this month when investors got nervous about its ability to finance its expansion plans and its bond yields leaped. Other major players, including Intel, Meta and Nvidia, have also been buffeted by concerns and watched their share prices slide in recent weeks.

Debt financing has been a growing concern as AI-related companies scramble to raise money to meet demand at a time when interest rates are poised to keep rising as the Federal Reserve tries to douse stubborn inflation.

The S-1 filing that tees up the IPO flagged what Anthropic sees as the risks from AI — and to its business model. Among them are the risk that its AI models could develop faster than the company can keep them safe, or that they could be used to cause harm — or take harmful actions on their own. It also flagged the risk of heightened scrutiny or political backlash for the company's views on policy and regulation.

Amodei himself has issued some of the AI world's sharpest warnings about the possibility of AI spiraling out of control and causing harm, and urged AI companies to "pace the frontier," or to slow the development of their most capable models.

Anthropic has also clashed with the Pentagon this year over how the military can use its models. Amodei has drawn a line in the sand when it comes to using Anthropic's AI for autonomous weapons and mass surveillance of Americans.

In response, the Pentagon blacklisted Anthropic and designated it a "supply chain risk" — a label previously reserved for entities affiliated with U.S. adversaries. Anthropic has sued the Pentagon in two federal district courts. Those legal battles remain ongoing.
articles.fullText:
Стартап искусственного интеллекта Anthropic, создатель чрезвычайно популярных моделей искусственного интеллекта Claude, сделал важный шаг к проведению первичного публичного предложения, которое, по мнению аналитиков, станет одним из крупнейших в истории.

В понедельник Anthropic подала окончательные документы в регулирующие органы на IPO под тикером ANT, который, по сообщениям, может стоить компании от 1,5 до 2 триллионов долларов.

Это поставило бы его в один ряд с ракетной компанией Илона Маска и компанией SpaceX, которая была оценена примерно в 1,8 триллиона долларов, когда она была включена в список в июне. В проспекте листинга Anthropic не указано, сколько акций предложит компания или в каком ценовом диапазоне.

Подача публичной версии заявления о регистрации под названием форма S-1 в Комиссию по ценным бумагам и биржам является важной вехой в стремительном росте Anthropic. Он был запущен всего пять лет назад группой исследователей OpenAI во главе с Дарио Амодеем, которые были обеспокоены тем, что эта компания, управляемая Сэмом Альтманом, не находится на пути к безопасному развитию ИИ.

С тех пор Anthropic стала крупнейшим конкурентом OpenAI, с некоторыми из наиболее широко используемых моделей ИИ на рынке. Но компания столкнулась с противоречиями, включая конфликт с Пентагоном по поводу того, как ее модели могут быть использованы, и вопросы о страшных предупреждениях Амодея о рисках ИИ.

Акции ИИ пострадали от волатильности

Подача заявок происходит в нестабильное время на фондовом рынке для компаний, связанных с ИИ, поскольку инвесторы колеблются между изобилием о положительном влиянии ИИ на экономику и беспокойством о безопасности и цунами инвестиций в технологию.

IPO, которое может состояться уже в ноябре, станет одним из самых ожидаемых публичных акций за последние годы. OpenAI, которая делает ChatGPT, также планирует IPO, но эти планы временно находятся на льду, и Альтман исключил листинг в этом году как «необдуманный» перед лицом проблем безопасности ИИ.

"Публикация имеет много преимуществ. Это приносит капитал для роста. Это облегчает вам привлечение дополнительного капитала в другом месте. И это дает возможность вашим существующим инвесторам обналичить деньги, - сказал Джим Анхель, доцент и специалист по рынкам в Джорджтаунском университете.

Но, добавил он, «есть опасения, что мы можем оказаться в пузыре ИИ». Мы находимся в очень динамичной отрасли, если не сказать больше, и мы можем ожидать большой волатильности на рынках». Тем не менее, по словам Анхеля, для Anthropic имеет смысл «ударить, пока железо горячо» и перечислить акции сейчас, чтобы получить как можно более высокую оценку.

Поскольку SpaceX уже торгует публично, IPO Anthropic может проверить аппетит инвесторов к предприятиям ИИ в то время, когда рынки беспокоятся о том, могут ли они быть достаточно прибыльными, чтобы оправдать ошеломляющие суммы денег, инвестируемые в ИИ. Акции SpaceX быстро взлетели после листинга, но вернулись примерно к 150 долларам, где они начали торговать.

Остаются опасения по поводу сектора ИИ

Балансирующий акт для компаний, пытающихся преодолеть волну ИИ, реален. Центр обработки данных и поставщик инфраструктуры CoreWeave в этом месяце столкнулись с падением цен на акции, когда инвесторы начали нервничать из-за возможности финансировать планы расширения, а доходность облигаций резко возросла. Другие крупные игроки, в том числе Intel, Meta и Nvidia, также были обеспокоены снижением цен на акции в последние недели.

Финансирование долга вызывает растущую озабоченность, поскольку компании, связанные с ИИ, пытаются собрать деньги для удовлетворения спроса в то время, когда процентные ставки готовы продолжать расти, поскольку Федеральная резервная система пытается обуздать упрямую инфляцию.

Подача заявки S-1, которая увеличивает IPO, отметила то, что Anthropic рассматривает как риски от ИИ и его бизнес-модели. Среди них есть риск того, что его модели ИИ могут развиваться быстрее, чем компания может обеспечить их безопасность, или что они могут быть использованы для причинения вреда. Кроме того, он отметил риск усиления контроля или политической реакции на взгляды компании на политику и регулирование.

Сам Амодей выпустил некоторые из самых резких предупреждений в мире ИИ о возможности выхода ИИ из-под контроля и причинения вреда, и призвал компании ИИ «продвигаться по границе» или замедлить разработку своих самых способных моделей.

В этом году Anthropic также столкнулась с Пентагоном по поводу того, как военные могут использовать свои модели. Амодей провел черту на песке, когда речь заходит об использовании ИИ Anthropic для автономного оружия и массового наблюдения за американцами.

В ответ Пентагон включил Anthropic в черный список и назвал его «риском цепочки поставок» — ярлыком, ранее зарезервированным для организаций, связанных с противниками США. Anthropic подала в суд на Пентагон в двух федеральных окружных судах. Эти правовые баталии продолжаются.

articles.originalTitle: Оппозиция Германии выставила жесткие требования Евросоюзу
articles.originalFullText:
Сопредседатель партии «Альтернатива для Германии» (АдГ) Алиса Вайдель пообещала провести референдум о выходе ФРГ из Европейского союза (ЕС), если страны-участницы объединения откажутся от его реформирования. Об этом сообщает британское издание The Telegraph.

«Мы хотим перестроить и реформировать Европейский союз. ЕС больше не является объединением суверенных государств. Национальные парламенты и правительства должны взять на себя процесс принятия решений»,— сказала она.

Вайдель заявила, что в случае отказа европейских стран от реформирования объединения Германия проведет референдум по вопросу выхода страны из Евросоюза по примеру Великобритании.

Ранее Алиса Вайдель заявила, что правительство ФРГ во главе с канцлером Фридрихом Мерцем должно уйти в отставку, поскольку оно не справляется с экономическими проблемами страны. По ее мнению, у действующих властей Германии был шанс исправить ошибки и стабилизировать экономическую ситуацию в стране, но они «потерпели крах по всем фронтам».

articles.originalTitle: На Западе указали на отчаянное положение Зеленского из-за предложения начать переговоры
articles.originalFullText:
Украинский лидер Владимир Зеленский предложил перейти к трехсторонним переговорам, осознавая, что их исход окажется неблагоприятным для Украины. Об этом заявил лидер французской партии «Народный республиканский союз», политолог Франсуа Асселино на своей странице в социальной сети X.

«Зеленский наконец согласился открыть переговоры с Россией, зная, что они, скорее всего, завершатся на ее условиях», — написал он.

По мнению Асселино, Украине придется изменить свою Конституцию, чтобы официально закрепить отказ от вступления в НАТО и признать передачу Крыма и Донбасса России.

Ранее президент России Владимир Путин обозначил тему трехсторонних переговоров по украинскому кризису, которые состоятся в Абу-Даби, — это вопросы безопасности для России и Украины после выхода на мирное урегулирование. Он отметил, что переговоры в Абу-Даби запланированы на первую половину ноября.

articles.originalTitle: Macron vows 'strong measures' to combat protests that rocked France
articles.originalText: French President Emmanuel Macron said his government will announce "strong measures" in response to violent protests in France in recent weeks. But he also acknowledged that students have "legitimate" grievances.
articles.originalFullText:
The French government is set to announce a series of "strong measures" to assuage protests which have rocked France in recent weeks, President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday.

Speaking in the southern city of Marseille, Macron warned that fresh demonstrations planned for this coming Saturday were "risky" and said that protest routes would remain outside city centers in order to protect public order.

France braces for 'lively' Halloween

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told broadcaster BFM that he was expecting further disturbances on October 31.

"Halloween evening is traditionally always a bit lively," he said. "We expect it to be complicated again."

Prior to Macron's arrival in Marseille, the Elysee Palace said the president intended to "pay tribute to and thank the internal security forces that helped restore republican order" in France's second-largest city where protesters briefly stormed the city hall on October 17.

He acknowledged that French authorities had "not anticipated at all" the scale of demonstrations which descended into widespread violence in looting in several major cities, leading to suggestions the state had lost control of the streets.

Macron: 'Social media is damaging our democracies'

The French president also highlighted the role of social media in the protests, saying the online networks were "damaging our democracies" by "bringing young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place."

He described social media as "tools for mobilizing the worst impulses."

While Macron admitted that French security forces underestimated the extent to which "extreme left forces" would meet up "so early in the day" on October 17, Interior Minister Nunez highlighted the phenomenon of organized far-right mobs confronting left-wing activists in several cities.

"We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out to defend businesses," he told BFM.

"In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organized formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement."

A presidential aide said Macron wanted to demonstrate that "the state is present, standing firm and fulfilling its mission to protect."

The president said that curfews enabled relative order to be maintained during last Saturday's protests (October 24), when authorities also deployed 70,000 police officers across the country, making 1,435 arrests.

"The state prevailed this weekend. The state was strong," government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon told RTL radio.

France: Macron acknowledges 'legitimate' student demands

Nevertheless, President Macron also said he had instructed his government, led by Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, to "respond to the legitimate demands that lie at the root of this social movement."

He said the government will soon announce several "concrete and huge" measures aimed at addressing student concerns over education and university admissions, following a nationwide consultation with high school and university student representatives.

"There are demands that must be heard and answered," confirmed government spokeswoman Bregeon.

"But to answer them, there is a prerequisite: a return to calm. We cannot have a functioning social dialogue in a climate of violence such as the one we experienced a week ago."
